executiveSummary: Analysis of 21 surveillance reports spanning October 2025 through May 2026 reveals multiple concurrent biological threats across the Americas and Europe. Avian Influenza A(H5N1), a BSL-3 select agent, has generated two separate PAHO epidemiological updates in the Americas region, indicating sustained zoonotic transmission risk and potential for human spillover events. The Southern Hemisphere is entering its 2026 respiratory season with simultaneous circulation of seasonal influenza, RSV, and other respiratory viruses, compounding public health burden. Additional threats include active dengue, chikungunya, mpox, yellow fever, measles, hantavirus, and pertussis outbreaks across the Americas, with ECDC reporting ongoing communicable disease threats across five consecutive weekly reports for Europe.
bottomLine: Avian Influenza A(H5N1) remains the highest-priority select agent threat in the Americas, compounded by simultaneous multi-pathogen respiratory season onset and widespread arboviral and vaccine-preventable disease activity.

threats.name: Avian Influenza A(H5N1)
signals: Two separate PAHO epidemiological updates issued November 2025 and March 2026 indicating sustained activity
BSL-3 select agent with documented zoonotic spillover potential and pandemic risk
Continued animal-to-human transmission risk across multiple Americas countries
Ongoing surveillance updates suggest evolving geographic spread
threats.action: Activate enhanced zoonotic surveillance protocols; ensure antiviral stockpile readiness; coordinate with agricultural and wildlife sectors; prepare pandemic influenza contingency plans

threats.name: Mpox

BSL-3 pathogen with ongoing multi-country spread in Americas
Sustained community transmission requiring continued monitoring
Potential clade differentiation concerns given global context
threats.action: Strengthen genomic sequencing to identify circulating clades; expand vaccination coverage for at-risk populations; enhance case detection and contact tracing across the Americas

threats.name: Yellow Fever

Vaccine-preventable disease with high case fatality rate in unvaccinated populations
Sylvatic transmission cycles pose ongoing risk in endemic zones
Alert status suggests cases above expected baseline

threats.name: Measles
signals: PAHO epidemiological alert issued February 3 2026
Vaccine-preventable disease indicating immunity gaps in the region
Americas region had achieved elimination status previously making resurgence a critical signal
Importation risks from endemic regions globally
threats.action: Audit measles vaccination coverage; implement catch-up campaigns in under-immunized communities; strengthen entry surveillance at international ports

threats.name: Pertussis (Whooping Cough)
signals: Two PAHO updates issued December 2025 and March 2026 indicating sustained multi-month activity
Resurgence pattern consistent with waning vaccine immunity in adolescents and adults
Infant mortality risk remains high in unvaccinated or partially vaccinated children
Dual-season reporting suggests endemic re-establishment
threats.action: Review Tdap booster coverage; strengthen maternal immunization programs; enhance laboratory confirmation capacity

threats.name: Hantavirus Pulmonary Syndrome
signals: PAHO epidemiological alert issued December 19 2025
Rodent reservoir activity associated with environmental and climate factors
High case fatality rate (30-40%) with no specific antiviral treatment available
Zoonotic transmission risk in rural and peri-urban areas
threats.action: Enhance rodent control programs in endemic areas; educate high-risk populations on exposure prevention; strengthen clinical recognition and rapid case reporting

selectAgentSummary: Two BSL-3 select agents were identified in this surveillance period. Avian Influenza A(H5N1) generated two PAHO epidemiological updates (November 2025 and March 2026) for the Americas region, indicating sustained zoonotic activity with pandemic potential and warranting Critical threat designation. Monkeypox virus (BSL-3) generated a PAHO update in April 2026 confirming ongoing mpox transmission in the Americas, designated Elevated given current epidemiological context. Both agents require enhanced biosafety protocols, accelerated genomic surveillance, and international coordination.
amrSignals: No explicit AMR reports identified in current surveillance batch; however Bordetella pertussis surveillance should include macrolide resistance screening given prolonged multi-season activity
Avian influenza antiviral resistance monitoring for oseltamivir should be maintained given sustained H5N1 circulation
emergingPatterns: Multi-pathogen respiratory convergence with simultaneous influenza, RSV, and other respiratory viruses circulating across Northern and Southern Hemisphere transition periods
Sustained arboviral burden with dengue, chikungunya, and yellow fever co-circulating in the Americas suggesting enhanced Aedes vector activity likely linked to climate conditions
Resurgence of historically controlled vaccine-preventable diseases (measles, pertussis) indicating immunity gaps and potential breakdown of routine immunization programs
Dual-season H5N1 alert pattern (November 2025 and March 2026) suggests persistent enzootic establishment rather than episodic incursion in Americas
GLP-1 receptor agonist medication misuse alert represents an emerging non-infectious public health signal intersecting with healthcare system capacity
